figures.alt: Thomas Holme's 1687 map of the improved part of Pennsylvania, showing surveyed parcels with owners' names along the Delaware River and a grid plan of Philadelphia in the inset
figures.caption: Holme's map of Pennsylvania (1687)

primary_sources: Thomas Holme, A Map of the Improved Part of the Province of Pennsylvania in America (1687)

options.misconception: A regular grid is a plan, not its absence — Penn laid the city out before anyone lived there.
options.text: Penn wanted Philadelphia to grow without any plan, like older English towns.

options.misconception: London's streets were famously irregular — the grid was Penn's own orderly design, not a copy.
options.text: Penn copied the street plan of London exactly.

options.misconception: The grid shows streets and squares, not walls and bastions — Philadelphia was a capital, not a fortress.
options.text: Penn planned Philadelphia as a fortress against Spanish Florida.
Penn intended an orderly, planned capital for his "Holy Experiment."

rationales.A: A regular grid is a plan, not the absence of one — Penn laid the city out before anyone lived there.
rationales.B: London's streets were crooked and medieval; the grid was Penn's own orderly design, not a copy.
rationales.C: The grid shows streets and squares, not walls and bastions — Philadelphia was a commercial capital, not a fortress.
rationales.D: The grid is the city drawn before it was built, the mark of a proprietor planning an orderly capital for his colony.
rationales.general:
1. Look at the inset. Streets cross at right angles, squares set in rows — a city drawn with a ruler.
2. Ask when a city looks like that. When it is planned on paper before it is built, not grown by accident.
3. Ask what Penn wanted. Background: Penn called Pennsylvania a 'Holy Experiment' — a place where Quakers could worship freely and live in order.
4. Name the link. The grid is the experiment made visible: a tidy city for a tidy, godly colony.
Remember: a planned city is a founder's values drawn on the ground, so read the streets as a statement.

source: original; stimulus image from the shared pool, Thomas Holme, A Map of the Improved Part of Pennsylvania (1687), public domain
stem: The inset in the upper right corner shows Philadelphia as a regular grid of streets. What does that grid best reflect about Penn's plan for his colony?

stimulus.source_note: Map from the shared image pool; Thomas Holme, A Map of the Improved Part of the Province of Pennsylvania in America (1687), public domain.
stimulus.text: Thomas Holme's map of the improved part of Pennsylvania, surveyed for William Penn and published in 1687. The map shows the Delaware River along the bottom and the settled land divided into surveyed parcels, each marked with an owner's name — Radnor, Haverford, Germantown, and many others. In the upper right corner, an inset shows the city of Philadelphia laid out as a regular grid of streets. The Penn coat of arms fills the upper left corner, and the map is dedicated to William Penn, proprietor of Pennsylvania.
